name: Bathroom Upgrades: How to Plan and Execute Your Renovation

step.name: Step 1: Assess existing moisture and room conditions
step.text: Inspect your subfloor, vanity drywall, and shower framing for hidden water damage or mold before ordering any finish products. Having an accurate look at concealed areas helps you establish a realistic scope of work.

step.name: Step 2: Finalize the layout and verify rough-in dimensions
step.text: Decide whether you want to preserve your current plumbing layout or relocate pipes, toilets, and drains to new locations. Measure your door clearings and rough-in spaces carefully to ensure your intended fixtures fit properly.

step.name: Step 3: Confirm electrical, plumbing, and mechanical requirements
step.text: Verify that your existing circuits meet requirements for dedicated GFCI outlets and modern exhaust ventilation capacity. Relocating major supply lines or adding high-draw fixtures may require local trade permits and inspections.

step.name: Step 4: Select and order all fixtures, tile, and trim
step.text: Purchase your vanity, waterproofing membranes, faucets, and tile before removing anything from the bathroom. Having specific model numbers and physical products on site prevents project standstills once walls are opened.

step.name: Step 5: Perform teardown and rough-in modifications
step.text: Strip old finishes down to sound framing, complete necessary plumbing updates, and pull updated electrical lines. The framing must be plumb, level, and structurally sound before closing the walls back up.

step.name: Step 6: Install waterproofing systems, finishes, and hardware
step.text: Hang cement board, apply waterproofing membranes to shower surrounds, set tile, and install cabinetry and light fixtures. Each layer needs full curing time before installing trim and fixtures.

step.name: Step 7: Conduct thorough leak checks and electrical tests
step.text: Run all water fixtures continuously to check every connection and drain trap for leaks, and test all electrical outlets for GFCI safety. Once fully tested, your bathroom is clean, secure, and ready for use. To review your bathroom remodel in the Denver area, contact Abraham Becerra at HH Remodeling LLC by calling 303-505-0866.
